questions.q: Why do unreferenced files pile up on disk over time in a Delta table?
options: Because a "remove" action (Lesson 17) doesn't delete a file immediately — it just marks it as no longer part of the current version
Delta automatically duplicates every file on every write
OPTIMIZE creates extra copies of every file it compacts
It only happens if schema enforcement is disabled
questions.explain: This is exactly what makes time travel possible, but it also means storage costs grow unless something cleans them up.

options: Permanently deletes files no longer referenced by the current version, but only ones older than the retention threshold
Compacts small files into larger ones, same as OPTIMIZE
Deletes every file in the table's folder immediately, regardless of age
Only marks files for deletion without ever removing them
questions.explain: The default retention threshold is 7 days — files younger than that are left alone even if unreferenced.

questions.q: Why is lowering VACUUM's retention window below the 7-day default risky?
options: A long-running query or concurrent job reading an older version can have files deleted out from under it mid-read, causing a real failure
It has no real risk; the default is just an arbitrary convention
It would make OPTIMIZE stop working entirely
It only affects tables using Unity Catalog
questions.explain: The 7-day default exists specifically to make that scenario unlikely in practice.

questions.q: What does VACUUM trips DRY RUN do?
options: Shows what would be deleted, without actually deleting anything
Permanently deletes all unreferenced files immediately
Runs OPTIMIZE instead of VACUUM
Only works on tables smaller than a certain size
questions.explain: This is a safe way to preview VACUUM's effect before committing to the real deletion.

questions.q: Why is VACUUM in direct tension with time travel?
options: Once VACUUM deletes a version's files, that version becomes genuinely unqueryable — this is exactly why time travel isn't a permanent backup
VACUUM actually extends how far back time travel can go
There's no real tension; the two features are completely unrelated
VACUUM only affects Unity Catalog volumes, not time travel
questions.explain: Real production tables balance retention length deliberately — long enough to be useful, short enough to bound storage costs.
